title: hello
description: First frame on the signaling connection, bench -> hub, sent right after the WebSocket opens. The credential is not in this frame: it rides the x-dhands-token header of the WebSocket upgrade. The hub answers hello_ok, or error (PROTO_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED / BAD_FRAME / UNKNOWN_VERB) followed by close code 1002. See sequences.md section 2.

bench_id.description: Stable identity of this bench. Must contain a non-blank character. Reconnecting with the same id replaces the previous registration.

name.description: Human-readable bench name; may be empty (the hub then shows bench_id).

impl.description: Which implementation of the bench program this is.

os.description: Operating system of the bench host.

ops.description: The bench op table, one OpDesc per op, names unique. What the bench can do follows from this table alone (there is no separate capability list): e.g. fastboot is available when the table has rows of group fastboot.

boards.description: Boards whose identity the bench checks before a write, keyed by board name (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$). Same shape as v1; a board description (type, ports) will be added as new optional fields without a version change.

partitions.description: Always null from the current bench (no list limits partition names). null means not configured, never 'none'.

product.description: What `fastboot getvar product` must answer before a write to this board.

update.description: Optional. Outcome of the last remote self-update as the bench's update helper recorded it; absent when there is none. The hub reads outcome=pending from a hello whose impl.build equals to_build as updated.
